content:
Former Liberal minister Philip Ruddock has been appointed by the Australian cabinet to examine whether current laws adequately protect religious freedom. The appointment was announced on Wednesday and is intended to prevent a contentious debate about religious amendments in the same-sex marriage bill.

***

The review has created division within the government. While some senior conservatives like Peter Dutton and Mathias Cormann believe a religious freedom bill can be considered separately next year, others including Treasurer Scott Morrison and Senator David Fawcett insist it must be addressed alongside the marriage bill. Morrison stated the review is "no substitute" for religious amendments.

***

Prime Minister Malcolm Turnbull emphasized the need for careful consideration of religious freedom issues following the yes vote on marriage equality. He noted that various proposals for legislative changes have been put forward recently, but many extend beyond the immediate marriage issue.

***

Turnbull warned against rushing legislative reforms, citing concerns about unintended consequences when parliament attempts to protect basic rights and freedoms. The government is particularly worried about creating uncertainties through broadly worded bill of rights-style declarations.

***

Ruddock has been asked to deliver his report by March 31. Turnbull described the review as a "timely expert stocktake" to inform any necessary legislative reforms and said Ruddock was well-suited for the role given his experience as Australia's special envoy for human rights.
